turns.text: Hi! In your own words, what is the problem asking you to find?
Um, how much money Patrick made selling lemonade for the whole 6 hours, I think.
Yes. How much money did he make in just one of the first four hours?
He sold 15 cups at fifty cents each, so that's 7.50 dollars?
Good. How many hours did he sell at that rate?
Four hours. So 7.50 times 4 is 30 dollars.
Nice. What happened in the next two hours?
He sold 10 cups at 60 cents, so that's 6 dollars an hour, and for two hours it's 12 dollars.
So you have 30 dollars and 12 dollars. What does the problem want you to do with those?
Add them, I guess, since it's the total for 6 hours. So 42 dollars.
Why does adding those two amounts give what Patrick earned in all 6 hours?
Because the first 4 hours and the next 2 hours are different parts of the 6 hours, so you put the money from both together.
Exactly, the two chunks cover all the hours with no overlap. [END]
